synopsis: Auto-GCAS takes control of F-16 and F-35 fighter aircraft and pulls them up when a ground collision is imminent [f15732]. F-35 integration occurred in 2019, which Lockheed Martin reported was seven years earlier than previously planned [f1443, f15735, f1917]. The manufacturer attributed this acceleration to agile development and reuse of earlier F-16 work; Chapter 2 and the glossary consistently repeat that account [f1443, f1568, f16423, f15735]. Lockheed Martin also credited Auto-GCAS with saving eight F-16 pilots’ lives by the time of F-35 integration, but that figure concerns F-16 outcomes rather than demonstrated F-35 outcomes [f1444]. The schedule acceleration and life-saving claims are vendor-attributed in the supplied facts, with no independent corroboration provided [f1443, f1444, f1917].
